source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. Core protection, retirement, scanning, bounds, progress, and ABA scope were checked against Michael's IEEE/PODC work; comparative limitations against Brown and Fraser; current standard/API shape against the C++ safe-reclamation draft, P2530R3, and Folly; and ordering/RCU context against the C++ atomic draft, Rustonomicon, and perfbook. Seven sources resolved directly, IEEE returned accepted metadata, and ACM publisher pages denied automated retrieval. Inaccessible publisher pages support bibliographic and scoped theorem attribution only, not quotations or unobserved details.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines source S, slots HP[i,j], protected set H, retire set Ret, candidate p, slot/participant counts K/P, threshold T, and reachable/retired/reclaimable predicates.
The chapter separates abstract removal, retirement ownership, hazard publication, validated access, scan absence, reclamation, reuse, and destruction.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checked set/list distinctions, state transitions, ownership terminology, asymptotic variables, and conditional progress language.

evidence: Example 6 recomputation: 64 participant records times two slots gives 128 scanned slots; 128 slot reads plus 256 retire entries gives 384 simplified units; 384/256=1.5 units per retirement.
artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-055/report.json records first-scan reclamation C, retention A, second-scan reclamation A, empty retirement, and exact-once reclaimed set A/C.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The unit-cost model is stipulated and explicitly excludes caches, synchronization, scheduling, and deleter cost.

evidence: If unlink precedes accepted validation, source revalidation rejects p; if accepted validation precedes unlink, correct scanner ordering retains p while its hazard remains published.
The simplified scan work O(P*K+|Ret|) follows from reading P records with K slots and partitioning the retire list once.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The safety split depends on the exact source-language order connecting source load, hazard store, validation, unlink, retirement, scan, clear, and delete.

evidence: Reviewed null, removal before publication, validation before removal, two readers, conservative scans, slot reuse, successor handoff, helping, double/missing retirement, and immediate address reuse.

Reviewed insufficient/exhausted records, thread pause/exit/death, local-list leakage, relaxed ordering, mutable payloads, blocking/re-entrant deleters, cancellation after unlink, scan storms, domain close/destruction, and high-stakes use.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis spans lifetime, logical ownership, ordering, progress, capacity, traversal, failure, lifecycle, observability, and safety consequences.

evidence: Every dereference maps to a validated live slot; each slot has one writer; clearing follows final access; traversal protects every simultaneously live separately reclaimable node.
Unlink precedes exactly-once retirement; scan deletes only retired addresses absent from every relevant hazard; exit and shutdown transfer/drain ownership before metadata destruction.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across acquire record, load, publish, validate, dereference, protect successor, retry, unlink, retire, scan, clear, reclaim, cancel, exit, close, and destroy.

evidence: The protection proof covers the exhaustive before/after relationship between removal and accepted validation and identifies the scanner visibility obligation in the latter case.
The reclamation argument combines no-new-acquisition after unlink, validation of pre-publication races, visibility of existing readers, exact-once retirement, and conservative retention.
proof_review.notes: This is a scoped internal proof review, not mechanized C++/Rust source refinement, weak-memory execution proof, allocator/deleter progress proof, or certification.

evidence: Lifetime safety, payload synchronization, data-structure linearizability, ABA resistance, bounded memory, progress, and performance remain separate claims.
The original-method properties are explicitly conditional on participant, slot, threshold, language-ordering, allocation, deletion, and target assumptions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Abstract mechanism, source implementation obligation, operational policy, empirical evidence, and human safety review are distinguishable.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-055 passed the deterministic retirement partition model with recorded interpreter version, exact stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit code.

The chapter requires schedule barriers, poisoned immediate reuse, sanitizer/model/weak-memory tests, target atomic inspection, pause/death/cancellation/shutdown stress, and capacity/lag/deleter telemetry.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The sequential model proves no concurrent visibility, lifetime safety, exact-once integration, weak-memory correctness, lock-free progress, bounded retention, performance, or deployment safety.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet foregrounds observation-versus-announcement; exposition derives the loop before infrastructure details; the scan model is reproducible; ten examples serve distinct purposes; and five exercises progress from the decisive race to surgical-robot transfer with complete matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external concurrency-theory, formal-methods, C++/Rust, compiler, architecture, allocator, memory-reclamation, operating-system, real-time, avionics, robotics, medical, regulatory, operational, or safety review is claimed.
